newsitem.title: USA: Killer of six in 1981 U.S. crime spree is executed.
newsitem.headline: Killer of six in 1981 U.S. crime spree is executed.

text.p: A man who said vengeance and a hatred of whites led him to slay six storekeepers in a weeklong 1981 crime spree was executed by lethal injection on Wednesday, prison authorities said.

Raymond Lee Stewart, 44, was convicted in 1982 of five of six murders he admitted to committing during a two-state crime spree that began on January 27, 1981, with four men shot to death in Illinois and two in Wisconsin.
Stewart was given a lethal injection just after midnight central time and died a short time later, said authorities at Stateville Correctional Centre in Joliet.

Earlier on Wednesday, Stewart was visited in his cell by Joseph Cardinal Bernardin, who prayed with him. The Chicago prelate, who recently announced he has terminal cancer, accepted the condemned killer's invitation to meet, although he did not perform last rites as Stewart was not Catholic.
"We talked about death. I told him we were in similar situations," Bernardin said.

Stewart's lawyers launched late appeals, arguing he was "warped beyond repair" by an abusive father and that prosecutors failed to properly inform jurors that a life sentence would have kept Stewart behind bars without possibility of parole. The appeals were denied.

Prosecutors said Stewart harboured a grudge against grocery store owner William Fredd for his testimony in Stewart's 1970 trial for armed robbery. He shot and killed Fredd and his nephew Albert Pearson.

The next day, Stewart killed a gas station attendant and made off with $72. The following day he killed another gas station attendant and then crossed into Wisconsin three days later where he murdered two workers at an electronics store in Beloit during a robbery. Stewart was arrested a month later.

A few days before his execution, Stewart said he had been motivated by a hatred of whites, whom he blamed for the assassinations of two of his heroes, civil rights leader the Rev. Martin Luther King Jr. and President John F. Kennedy.

During his murder trial in Rockford, Stewart bolted as he was being escorted back to court and hid in an oil drum for an hour before he was found, bleeding from a gunshot wound in the back sustained during his brief escape.
Stewart became the eighth person executed in Illinois since the state reinstated the death penalty in 1977.
